name: structural-ecoli
title: Structural E. coli
description:
Reconstructs a 3D structural view of the E. coli cell directly from a live
baseline whole-cell run, using the ecoli_structural composite (baseline +
an EcoliPackStep that packs the molecular state at declared simulation times).
First study saves two snapshots — an initial state ~10 s in and a pre-division
state — for the Analysis Tools Parsimony Viewer.

glossary.definition: The condensed, membrane-less region occupied by the E. coli chromosome; it excludes ribosomes and sets much of the cell's internal spatial structure.
The cell-cycle snapshot taken once a newborn cell has settled after division -- one of the two declared times packed into 3D.
The state captured just before the cell divides, when it is longest and its replicated chromosome is segregating -- the second declared time.
Placing the model's molecular counts into an explicit cell-shaped volume (respecting the envelope and nucleoid) so an implicit count vector becomes a viewable spatial arrangement.
The 3D viewer in which the packed declared-time snapshots are rendered and explored.

biological_story:
An E. coli cell is not a well-mixed bag: its molecules occupy an ~2 um rod with distinct spatial organization. The chromosome condenses into a nucleoid that excludes ribosomes toward the poles and periphery; ribosomes and most translation crowd the cytoplasm around it; membrane proteins and transporters sit in the inner membrane; and the arrangement changes over the cell cycle as the chromosome replicates and segregates and the cell elongates toward division.

The whole-cell model tracks molecular counts but is spatially implicit -- it knows how many of each molecule exist, not where. This investigation gives those counts a body: it packs the simulated molecular inventory into a 3D cell envelope at two declared cell-cycle times -- just after birth (post-equilibration) and just before division -- so the abstract state vector can be seen as a physical cell and inspected in the Parsimony Viewer. It is a visualization/spatialization layer over the existing dynamics, not a new spatial simulation.
question:
What does the whole-cell molecular state look like in real 3D space at key
points in the cell cycle — just after birth (post-equilibration) versus right
before division? Can we pack the simulated molecular counts into a 3D cell and
view declared-time snapshots in the Parsimony Viewer?

executive.what_is_this:
Reconstruct the whole-cell E. coli molecular state as a 3D structural view
directly from a live baseline run, packed into a gram-negative envelope at
two declared cell-cycle times (birth ~10 s, pre-division) and viewed in the
Parsimony Viewer. Single member study s01.
executive.verdict:
Concept demonstrated; headline numbers NOT reproducible/verified in the
canonical env. Gap closed by this hardening: s01 went from "ran, no gate,
uncommitted artifacts" to a defined, artifact-derived acceptance gate with
the reproducible core (snapshot scheduling + selection-layer count
conservation) verified GREEN, and the end-to-end pack gate implemented but
skipping until the pack toolchain is pinned and present. The 287k/552k
placed-instance numbers are from a prior run on a newer toolchain and were
NOT re-derived — the packs were never committed and the pack pipeline
(newer pbg-parsimony API + `parsimony` binary) is absent from the canonical
environment (4 structural tests RED on main).

studies.name: s01-birth-and-division
studies.question:
Pack the simulated whole-cell molecular state into a 3D cell at ~10 s
(post-equilibration birth) and right before division, so the Parsimony Viewer
can show both declared-time snapshots for this study.
